ucs.title: [LLM] Turla (Secret Blizzard) ComRAT v4 / Crutch — covert C2 via Gmail web UI and Dropbox API from non-browser process
ucs.description: Hunts for the signature Turla cloud-service C2 channel: ComRAT v4 reuses cookies to drive mail.google.com through the web UI (commands hidden in drafts/attachments), while the Crutch backdoor uses content.dropboxapi.com / api.dropboxapi.com to stage commands and exfil. Connections to these endpoints from any process other than known browsers/sync clients is a near-actor-unique tell.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime FROM datamodel=Web.Web WHERE (Web.dest IN ("mail.google.com","content.dropboxapi.com","api.dropboxapi.com","www.googleapis.com") OR Web.url="*mail.google.com*" OR Web.url="*dropboxapi.com*") AND NOT Web.app IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","outlook.exe","dropbox.exe","onedrive.exe","teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","slack.exe","thunderbird.exe") BY Web.src Web.user Web.app Web.dest Web.url Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | where user!="unknown" AND NOT match(user,"\\$$")
ucs.kql:
// Turla ComRAT v4 (Gmail) + Crutch (Dropbox) — non-browser / non-sync-client process reaching the covert C2 surface
let LegitCloudClients = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","safari.exe","outlook.exe","dropbox.exe","onedrive.exe","onedrivestandaloneupdater.exe","teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","slack.exe","thunderbird.exe"]);
let Cloud_C2_Hosts = dynamic(["mail.google.com","content.dropboxapi.com","api.dropboxapi.com","api-content.dropbox.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemoteUrl has_any (Cloud_C2_Hosts)
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (LegitCloudClients))
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
// pivot LOLBins + script hosts + user-writable launchpads — ComRAT/Crutch loaders live here
| extend Suspicious = InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","msbuild.exe","installutil.exe")
           or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\Windows\Temp\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Suspicious
| order by Timestamp desc

           or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\Windows\Temp\")

ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Turla ComRAT/Crutch cloud C2 from non-browser process
id: 8c2a7b3e-1f4d-4f9c-bf2a-7d3e5b1c9a01
status: experimental
description: Detects non-browser/non-sync processes establishing connections to mail.google.com or *.dropboxapi.com, consistent with Turla (Secret Blizzard) ComRAT v4 (Gmail web UI C2) and Crutch (Dropbox API C2) tradecraft.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/2020/05/26/agent-comrat-evolution-turla-mosquito/
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/2020/12/02/turla-crutch-keeping-back-door-dropbox/
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/05/29
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationHostname|contains:
      - 'mail.google.com'
      - 'content.dropboxapi.com'
      - 'api.dropboxapi.com'
      - 'api-content.dropbox.com'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '\opera.exe'
      - '\iexplore.exe'
      - '\outlook.exe'
      - '\dropbox.exe'
      - '\onedrive.exe'
      - '\teams.exe'
      - '\slack.exe'
      - '\thunderbird.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Custom in-house apps integrated with Gmail/Dropbox via OAuth (allowlist by hash)
  - PowerShell-based DevOps scripts that exfil to Dropbox
level: high
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1102.002
  - attack.t1567.002
  - attack.g0010
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(mail.google.com OR content.dropboxapi.com OR api.dropboxapi.com OR api-content.dropbox.com) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\MsEdge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\Firefox.exe OR *\\brave.exe OR *\\Brave.exe OR *\\opera.exe OR *\\iexplore.exe OR *\\IEXPLORE.EXE OR *\\outlook.exe OR *\\OUTLOOK.EXE OR *\\dropbox.exe OR *\\Dropbox.exe OR *\\onedrive.exe OR *\\OneDrive.exe OR *\\teams.exe OR *\\Teams.exe OR *\\ms-teams.exe OR *\\slack.exe OR *\\Slack.exe OR *\\thunderbird.exe)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^(mail\.google\.com|content\.dropboxapi\.com|api\.dropboxapi\.com|api-content\.dropbox\.com)$/i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera|iexplore|outlook|dropbox|onedrive|teams|ms-teams|slack|thunderbird)\.exe$/i)
| Suspicious := if(ContextImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|rundll32|regsvr32|mshta|wscript|cscript|wmic|msbuild|installutil)\.exe$/i, "true", "false")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, Suspicious], function=[count(), min(@timestamp, as=firstSeen), max(@timestamp, as=lastSeen)])
ucs.rationale: Both ComRAT v4 (ESET, May 2020) and Crutch (ESET, Dec 2020) are publicly attributed to Turla/Secret Blizzard and share the same operational signature: a custom loader (PowerShell stager, rundll32 DLL, or service binary) speaking HTTPS to a legitimate consumer cloud service. ucs.title: [LLM] Turla LightNeuron — Microsoft Exchange Transport Agent persistence install
ucs.description: Hunts the installation footprint of Turla's LightNeuron Exchange backdoor: a malicious managed Transport Agent DLL + winex.tlb + EdgeTransport.exe.config modification dropped under the Exchange TransportRoles\agents directory by a process other than the legitimate installer chain. Transport Agent persistence on Exchange is an actor-unique TTP — LightNeuron is the only publicly documented APT toolkit using it.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem WHERE (Filesystem.file_path="*\\TransportRoles\\agents\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Exchange Server\\V15\\TransportRoles\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Exchange Server\\V14\\TransportRoles\\*") AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.dll" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.tlb" OR Filesystem.file_name="EdgeTransport.exe.config") AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","setup.exe","Microsoft.Exchange.Setup.WindowsInstaller.exe","UMWorkerProcess.exe","ServiceHub.exe") BY Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | join type=outer dest, process_name [| tstats summariesonly=true count FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Processes WHERE Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND (Processes.process="*Install-TransportAgent*" OR Processes.process="*Enable-TransportAgent*" OR Processes.process="*New-TransportAgent*") BY Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process_name as install_proc, process as install_cmd]

title: Turla LightNeuron Exchange Transport Agent persistence

status: experimental
description: Detects DLL/TLB/config writes to the Microsoft Exchange TransportRoles\agents directory by a process outside the legitimate Exchange installer chain, consistent with Turla LightNeuron backdoor installation (ESET, May 2019).
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/2019/05/07/turla-lightneuron-email-too-far/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0395/
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/05/29
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:

    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\TransportRoles\agents\'
      - '\Exchange Server\V15\TransportRoles\'
      - '\Exchange Server\V14\TransportRoles\'

    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.dll'
      - '.tlb'
      - 'EdgeTransport.exe.config'

    Image|endswith:

      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\setup.exe'
      - '\Microsoft.Exchange.Setup.WindowsInstaller.exe'
      - '\UMWorkerProcess.exe'
      - '\ServiceHub.exe'

falsepositives:
  - Exchange CU/SU patching outside TrustedInstaller (rare; correlate to MS update process)
  - Authorised third-party transport agents (antispam/DLP) — allowlist by file hash + vendor
level: critical
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1505.002
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.g0010
  - attack.s0395
